title: Battery prices since 1991: true or myth?
subtitle: Four claims about lithium-ion batteries, true or myth? Two hosts argue each one, then the price of an electric car's battery in 1991.
shape: 3 + 6 (myth or true chain, two voices; b the confident wrong guesser)
form: quiz on canvas (True/Myth run over a sequence)
notes: Reworked after review from a bar drag into a True/Myth chain. All four claims from the OWID article (Ritchie & Rosado 2026): $9,200/kWh (1991) to $78 (2024), >99%; cumulative production ×27 million 1991–2023 and prices fell as more were made; early-1990s decline much slower (tiny market, Sony near-monopoly); EV cells ~$5,000 today, over $20,000 a decade ago. $600,000 = $5,000 × 9,200/78, my arithmetic, said as close to. The sequence label sat in the caption band at its default place; at.y 455 lifts it. Cast-level feedback lines; affirm playful.
